clue.text: Remunerative and it makes the expert healthy and competent

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
fit means in good health
able means competent

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased that a well-paid job suits the skilled, fit and capable.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something that brings in money or yields gain.

clue.text: Without me a tragic woman provides means of death

indicators.note: without tells us to drop the word me from the woman's name

parts.note: Merope is the tragic heroine of Matthew Arnold's verse drama of that name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tragic heroine, freed of the speaker, offers a way to die.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ME from MEROPE leaves the letters wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose of cord is a classic instrument of hanging, so of execution.

clue.text: The final issue is a note before half-term

indicators.note: before places the note ahead of the other piece

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: half of the word term means its first two of four letters

explanation.surface: A school report arrives just before the mid-term break, deciding everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Destiny is the ultimate outcome or issue of events.

clue.text: Part of body where you give a woman a kiss

parts.note: Thora is a woman's name
X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks where on the body one should kiss a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: The chest region of the body, between neck and abdomen.

clue.text: Gas-bag lawyers speak passionately for the defence

parts.note: a balloon is a bag filled with gas
the Bar is the body of barristers
to rage is to speak with fury

explanation.surface: A windbag barrister holds forth fervently in court for the accused.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts us in court with defence counsel; in fact the defence is anti-aircraft protection from tethered balloons, as used over Britain in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines of tethered balloons were a wartime protection against low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: Group which includes most of the new article in the finish

indicators.note: in places the other pieces inside the word for the finish

parts.note: the end is the finish

indicators.note: most of the word new drops its final letter

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A team contains most of the new item at the finishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims the last letter from 'new'; 'in' then sets that pair and the article within the finish, after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of nine, as in Plotinus's Enneads, is a particular grouping.

clue.text: The ruler is in if one starts a riot

indicators.note: is in says the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: The monarch is at home if somebody begins a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: The ruler is concealed across 'starTS A Riot'; 'if one' is linking padding.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor of Russia was a supreme ruler.

clue.text: Entertainment which provides evidence of promotion without drink

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the stripe goes around the drink

teas are drinks

explanation.surface: A soldier's sober show proves he got promoted without touching a drop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking'; it is the old sense 'outside', and the plural drink is a light stretch for the singular printed.
explanation.definitionFit: A burlesque act of undressing is a form of show or entertainment.

clue.text: Going about with a revolutionary Irishman?

parts.note: Pat is a stock Irish name
rolling means turning over and over, revolving

explanation.surface: Someone wanders round with an Irish rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' suggests a rebel, but it means revolving.
explanation.definitionFit: Policing an area means touring it on rounds.

clue.text: It takes an old penny paper to be tedious

parts.note: d was the abbreviation for a pre-decimal British penny
a rag is a low-grade newspaper

explanation.surface: A cheap tabloid costing a penny is boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that go on too slowly are said to be wearisome.

clue.text: Gold appearing, on a woman in what is natural but excessive

indicators.note: in places gold and the woman inside the natural word

parts.note: innate means inborn, natural

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so gold comes first

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
Di is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Gold jewellery on a lady looks natural yet over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond reasonable limits, immoderate.

clue.text: Monthly examination for the local dignitary

parts.note: May is a month
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: A regular monthly test for the town's leading figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the civic head of a town.

clue.text: For instance in a person about to provide explosive unit

indicators.note: in puts the example abbreviation inside the man
about means the man goes around the little word to

parts.note: a man is a person
taken as written
eg is the abbreviation for for example

explanation.surface: A man is about to deliver something explosive, as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'about' sets the little word inside the person after its second letter, then 'in' puts the example abbreviation after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure of bomb yield equal to a million tons of TNT.

clue.text: Note you on the left propagated

parts.note: la is a sol-fa note
ye is an old form of you
reds are the political left

explanation.surface: A message tells someone they are leaning politically leftward.
explanation.walkthrough: Gardeners propagate plants by layering, pegging a shoot into soil to root.
explanation.definitionFit: Layering is a gardener's method of plant propagation.

clue.text: Swindle and cause distress for the curved

parts.note: a con is a swindle
to vex is to annoy or distress

explanation.surface: A fraud that upsets those who are bent.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulging outwards like the outside of a sphere.

clue.text: Messages caught by efficient measures

parts.note: c is the cricket abbreviation for caught
able means capable, efficient
grams are units of weight

explanation.surface: Signals intercepted by smart measuring devices.
explanation.definitionFit: Telegrams sent by undersea cable are messages.

clue.text: Writer needs follow mother to prevent being dry

indicators.note: follow puts the writer after the mother

parts.note: a dam is an animal mother
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A writer must take after a mother to avoid dull prose.
explanation.definitionFit: To moisten something stops it staying parched.

clue.text: Titled person about to win over humble people where goods are cheap

indicators.note: about means the baronet goes round the rest

parts.note: Bart is the abbreviation for a baronet

indicators.note: over puts gaining before the lowly people

parts.note: to gain is to win
base men are people of low station

explanation.surface: A baronet tries to win over the lower orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the baronet's abbreviation round both gaining and the lowly men; 'to' belongs to the win, not to linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A store's lowest floor where reduced-price items are sold.

clue.text: Inventor gives back end of game

parts.note: no side is the referee's call ending a rugby match

explanation.surface: An inventor returns the final whistle.
explanation.walkthrough: NO SIDE is the old rugby term for the end of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Alva, the American who devised the phonograph and electric light bulb.

clue.text: Trance gives me something enjoyed by gods

explanation.surface: A trance hands me a heavenly treat.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink of the Olympians in Greek myth.

taken as written
